title: Oficio del Sumo Sacerdote Presidente
context: This section outlines the role and responsibilities of the President of the High Priesthood in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. It includes details on how he leads other priesthood holders, administers church affairs, and acts as a judge in Israel.

keyPoints.point: The President of the High Priesthood is called the 'Sumo Sacerdote Presidente' or 'President of the High Priesthood'.
He has the responsibility to preside over the administration of ordinances and blessings for the church, through laying on of hands.
An 'bishop' is not equal in this sense because his role is primarily temporal matters; however, a bishop may be chosen from those with the High Priesthood unless he is a literal descendant of Aaron.
In some cases, a non-descendant of Aaron can serve as an administrator and judge in Israel if apart from the president of the high priesthood.
Disputes regarding church matters are resolved through the Council of the High Priesthood or the Twelve counselors to it if necessary.
This section outlines a hierarchical structure for priesthood holders, from deacons to high priests, each presided over by their respective presidents.
